  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/bbc/simorgh/issues/3494",
  "title": "We don't know where our users are",
  "body": "Blocking https://github.com/bbc/psammead/issues/1957 being used in simorgh\r\n\r\n**Describe the bug**\r\nWhen simorgh was news articles only, we determined where a user was from a `BBC-ORIGIN` header sent from mozart. We use `headers['bbc-origin']` such that if it ends in `.co.uk` theyre in the UK, so show them the non-adverts cookie banner, else, show them the adverts cookie banner.\r\n\r\nSince simorgh has expanded out to the WS sites we lost use of this logic, as you can only hit them on `.com`, so you can only ever see the advert cookie banner.\r\n\r\nLuckily, this is the safest state to be in, as were showing messaging to people who dont need it, vs not showing it to people who do.\r\n\r\n**To Reproduce**\r\nSteps to reproduce the behavior:\r\n\r\nIn & Out of the UK\r\n1. Go to https://www.bbc.com/igbo\r\n2. See international cookie banner messaging\r\n\r\n**Expected behavior**\r\nIt shows the UK messaging if the user is inside the UK, even on `.com`\r\n\r\n**Possible fix implementation:**\r\nInstead of, or as well as the `bbc-origin` header, get an `isUK` header from mozart. This then needs to be baked into the page inside simorgh data, so on the client we know if theyre in or out of the UK (in place of fig). This info can then be used to show the right banner messaging and in future, adverts/not\r\n\r\n\r\n**Testing notes**\r\n\r\n- [x] This bug fix is expected to need manual testing.\r\n\r\n**Additional context**\r\nAdd any other context about the problem here.\r\n",

{
  "format": "coda-github-issue-snapshot",
  "format_version": 1,
  "artifact_id": "privacy-issue-linked-joomla-projects-privacy-framework-213",
  "issue_url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "source_issue_url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213",
  "title": "Missing consent \"evidence\" on contact form",
  "body": "Currently, when an user submits a request through the Contact Form he/she's prompted to grant a consent to process the request thanks to the new plugin, so the user has to flag the checkbox to proceed. And that's ok, but site owner must be able to demonstrate that the user gave his/her consent to process the request/data. \r\n\r\n### Describe the solution you'd like\r\nWe could have two opportunities:\r\n\r\n1. Add a copy of the consent statement in the email that is sent through the Contact Form.\r\n2. Record the consent in the Consent view within Privacy Dashboard (index.php?option=com_privacy&view=consents) \r\n\r\n",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2018-07-16T07:50:42Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:21:27.187037+00:00",
  "comments_fetched_at": [
    "2026-11-05T07:21:27.187037+00:00"
  ],
  "expected_comment_count": 26,
  "retrieved_comment_count": 26,
  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 405175249,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405175249",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T08:11:39Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T08:11:39Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "the fact that it is a required field is the evidence that the person consented.\r\n\r\nrecording the consent in the privacy dashboard is pointless as this contact form can be submitted by guest users"
    },
    {
      "id": 405182688,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405182688",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T08:47:36Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T08:47:36Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> recording the consent in the privacy dashboard is pointless as this contact form can be submitted by guest users\r\n\r\nThat is true.\r\n\r\n> the fact that it is a required field is the evidence that the person consented.\r\n\r\nThat would not so easy to bring as argument. It would be much better to have the statement in the email that is sent after form submission. "
    },
    {
      "id": 405186246,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405186246",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T09:02:32Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T09:02:32Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "do you require and record a consent before someone sends you an email?"
    },
    {
      "id": 405187421,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405187421",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T09:07:39Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T09:07:39Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Nope. But, if someone sends me a message through the website, i need to demonstrate that the user read and accepted the privacy policy shown on the website."
    },
    {
      "id": 405202243,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405202243",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T10:10:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T10:10:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "And com_contact doesn't store information in the DB, so I don't think it's needed to keep track of their consent in the DB (and then in that case you are finally storing their data)"
    },
    {
      "id": 405204084,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405204084",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T10:19:09Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T10:19:08Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> And com_contact doesn't store information in the DB, so I don't think it's needed to keep track of their consent in the DB (and then in that case you are finally storing their data)\r\n\r\nThat's why having a \"confirmation text\" in the email would be the perfect way to achieve it."
    },
    {
      "id": 405223940,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405223940",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T11:57:58Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T11:57:57Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "There is no hook system to alter emails, so without hardcoding things into com_contact, we can't change any email contents."
    },
    {
      "id": 405224389,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405224389",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:00:06Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:00:06Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> There is no hook system to alter emails, so without hardcoding things into com_contact, we can't change any email contents.\r\n\r\nIn this case i believe that hardcoding something like the following sentence is not so bad:\r\n\r\n `The user accepted the privacy policy to process this request on DATE`"
    },
    {
      "id": 405226720,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405226720",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:08:14Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:08:14Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Not really.  It would only be true if the plugin asking consent is enabled and all the pre-conditions involving that has been set.  Even then, that means hardcoding a plugin's configuration into a component, which is not proper system design (a component should not be aware of a specific plugin's presence at all)."
    },
    {
      "id": 405227935,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405227935",
      "created_at": "2018-07-16T12:13:51Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-16T12:13:51Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "You can't hard code it into the email because not all sites will require the consent"
    },
    {
      "id": 405557100,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405557100",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T11:59:38Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T11:59:38Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "I would see the situation in the following way: The spirit of GDPR is to make it obvious to the user what data a website collects about a person. In the case of a contact form, all data is provided by the user. So the consent of the user is given the moment that he typed it into the form. It is also not required that the user typed in real data. Long story short: For now I would say that the implicit consent was given when the contact form was filled out and the explicit consent was given when the checkbox was checked. That explicit consent is implicitly stored by the timestamp of the send mail.\r\n\r\nSo I would vote against coding anything into this and close this issue.\r\n\r\nOne thing that would also speak against storing this in Joomla would be, that sites without any interactive elements except for this contact form (like my own website for example) would then have to set up the whole privacy component. Right now a person could request all the data that I have about it and I would only have to go through the stuff on my local system. When you are storing this data in Joomla, you would have to provide that export, too.\r\n\r\nSo, nothing to do here, at least for now. We could revisit this issue when there are the first few decisions by courts."
    },
    {
      "id": 405579471,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405579471",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:21:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:21:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Personally, i don't think we should store the consent in the Privacy dashboard.\r\nPursuant the Italian Law, before GDPR, there was a similar \"consent\" mechanism that each website should have implemented and generally it has been done through a checkbox at the end of the contact form (obviously people used third-party extensions to achieve this).\r\nThe checkbox was something similar to \"I agree with the Privacy Policy of this website\" and this sentence was copied also in the email sent to the administrator.\r\nSomething like this has been mandatory in Italy (at least) from several years. \r\nAccording to GDPR, consents must always be explicit, clear, with clear purpose and so on... so even if i agree with you that if i contact you, i'm implicitly consenting you to process the data i submit, it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence."
    },
    {
      "id": 405583564,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405583564",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:34:13Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:34:13Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "> it would be good, if we can add to the email the consent sentence.\r\n\r\nIt would be nice.  Our system capabilities do not allow us to do so without hardcoding com_contact to be dependent on the single privacy consent plugin that we ship in core.  We do not have a hook to alter emails when they are being sent in core, and arbitrarily adding the string to the email would be factually incorrect if you do not have any form of consent in place when submitting it."
    },
    {
      "id": 405586341,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405586341",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:42:52Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:42:52Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> Our system capabilities do not allow us to do so without hardcoding com_contact to be dependent on the single privacy consent plugin that we ship in core.\r\n\r\nI fully understand this. And what about extending com_contact instead of using the plugin?"
    },
    {
      "id": 405587962,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405587962",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T13:47:44Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T13:47:44Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "The only other option is to remove the consent plugin and put options in every component to do the same thing that the consent plugin is doing.  Then, because the options are within the component, could you alter the email body string conditionally without breaking any system rules."
    },
    {
      "id": 405595557,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405595557",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:10:21Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:10:21Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> The only other option is to remove the consent plugin and put options in every component to do the same thing that the consent plugin is doing.\r\n\r\nFor the contact form, i believe that would be appropriate and would satisfy the requirement."
    },
    {
      "id": 405598622,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405598622",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:19:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:19:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "1. this is not a gdpr solution\r\n2. This is just to help you along the way\r\n3. We can never address every countries unique interpretation of a law\r\n4. What were italian web sites doing before "
    },
    {
      "id": 405599569,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405599569",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T14:21:53Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T14:21:53Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Making any changes for this specific if/else condition IMO opens too many cans of worms to reliably manage, because the scope of work I see it creating ends up in creating a lite version of com_content in com_privacy to have a single spot in core to define and manage the privacy policy (because you can't reasonably force com_contact to only support a com_content created privacy policy article)."
    },
    {
      "id": 405615057,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405615057",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T15:03:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T15:03:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> What were italian web sites doing before\r\n\r\nUsing different contact forms components.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 405645312,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405645312",
      "created_at": "2018-07-17T16:31:16Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-17T16:31:16Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "You are giving explicit consent to this when checking the checkbox. You are logging if the plugin is active in our actionlog. So you can say \"The user had to check the checkbox, otherwise the mail wouldn't have been sent and the checkbox was built in and working, because we have the enabling/disabling of the plugin logged in our log.\""
    },
    {
      "id": 405875874,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405875874",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T09:49:35Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T09:49:35Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "@jeckodevelopment\r\nYou can solve the problem by using the custom fields in this way ...\r\n\r\n1 - Create a new group of \"mail\" type fields and name it \"Privacy policy\".\r\n\r\n2 - Create a new additional field of type \"mail\" as follows:\r\n\r\nTitle > I declare that I have read and accepted the following Privacy policy\r\n\r\nType > Checkboxes\r\n\r\nRequired > Yes\r\n\r\nText > By sending us a message through this form, or by directly using the e-mail address indicated here, the processing of your personal data will be carried out in compliance with the EU Regulation 2016/679. The personal data you have provided may be processed in compliance with the aforementioned legislation. The Data Controller, in compliance with the Regulations, will take care of archiving for purposes consistent with the interactions shown by the Visitor and only for the time strictly necessary for the verification and evaluation of the information provided, for the purpose of exchanging information or contacts. To find out more about our privacy policies, please see the extended information at https://www.XXXXXXXXXXXXXXX/privacy. To request information, changes, or to oppose the treatment and request the cancellation of your data, present in our archives, you can write to us via the address XXXXXXXXXX@XXXXXXX.XX.\r\n\r\nValue > The same policy entered in Text\r\n\r\nField Group > Assign the previously created group \"Privacy policy\".\r\n\r\nGo to the Permissions tab and set this...\r\nEdit Custom Field Value > Allowed\r\n\r\nIn this way, the privacy policy will be visible on the contact page, but will also be contained in the email."
    },
    {
      "id": 405877618,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405877618",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T09:55:53Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T09:55:52Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "thanks @linuxpac , but i wasn't really looking for a solution for that :)\r\nMy suggestion was to implement the opportunity to add the statement into com_contact. \r\nAnyway, if you guys think that it's not necessary, feel free to close the issue.\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 405884419,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-405884419",
      "created_at": "2018-07-18T10:21:45Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-07-18T10:21:45Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "Ok, jeckodevelopment. However, this solution works well and also allows you to demonstrate that the visitor has read and accepted the policy (if you have activated the function \"Send Copy to Submitter\", even the sender will receive the email containing the declaration of acceptance of the policy with the policy itself)."
    },
    {
      "id": 409890580,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-409890580",
      "created_at": "2018-08-02T11:07:50Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-02T11:07:50Z",
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "It's easy to add such a phrase to the email body of the contact form with a small 3rd plugin. I didn't think too much about it but something like this should work:\r\n```\r\n public function onSubmitContact(&$contact, &$data)\r\n {\r\n  if (JPluginHelper::isEnabled('content', 'confirmconsent'))\r\n  {\r\n   if (isset($data['consentbox']) && !empty($data['consentbox']))\r\n   {\r\n    $data['contact_message'] .= \"\\n\\n\" . 'The user accepted the privacy policy to process this request on DATE';\r\n   }\r\n   // Nearly impossible(?):\r\n   else\r\n   {\r\n    // Say this \r\n   }\r\n  }\r\n  else\r\n  {\r\n   // Say that\r\n  }\r\n  return true;\r\n }\r\n```"
    },
    {
      "id": 411257564,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-411257564",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-08T01:51:03Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Closing this out.  Given the core architectural changes needed to properly support this it is too far out of scope to include here, and as pointed out it is possible to add this statement via plugin if so desired."
    },
    {
      "id": 411301558,
      "url": "https://github.com/joomla-projects/privacy-framework/issues/213#issuecomment-411301558",
      "created_at": "2018-08-08T06:34:48Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-08-08T06:34:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Thanks"
    }
  ],

{ "format": "coda-github-issue-snapshot", "format_version": 1, "artifact_id": "privacy-issue-linked-2745", "issue_url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745", "source_issue_url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745", "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745", "title": "NVDA + Firefox alerts not working properly", "body": "**Reported by javis on 2012-10-25 16:09**\r\nThe following markup does not work properly with NVDA + Firefox.\r\n\r\n```\r\n
\r\n
\r\n My Message\r\n
\r\n
\r\n```\r\n\r\nNVDA will only read \"Alert\" but not the text inside of the DIV. It seems that NVDA only reads the first child element and then ignores the rest of the content. This same markup works fine with IE + NVDA.\r\n", "author": "Participant 1", "created_at": "2012-10-25T16:09:35Z", "updated_at": "2025-01-16T16:39:19Z", "state": "closed", "closed_at": null, "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:17:34.699307+00:00", "comments_fetched_at": [ "2026-11-05T07:17:34.699307+00:00", "2026-11-05T07:17:42.016946+00:00" ], "expected_comment_count": 24, "retrieved_comment_count": 25, "comments_complete": false, "comments": [ { "id": 155301256, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-155301256", "created_at": "2012-10-25T23:17:04Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 1", "body": "Comment 1 by jteh on 2012-10-25 23:17\nNVDA uses the same code it uses to get text from dialogs. It's rather complicated, but in short, it tries to find all descendants that might be text. However, it does not descend into certain objects including sections (which is what divs are mapped to in Firefox) because they normally don't contain dialog text. We need to think on how to fix this without breaking other use cases.\n" }, { "id": 155301257, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-155301257", "created_at": "2012-10-26T18:24:10Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 1", "body": "Comment 3 by javis on 2012-10-26 18:24\nJust wanted to add a quick note to this one. It also looks like if you swap out the DIV for a span it will work. However, if your span has either position:fixed or display:block it will stop working.\n\nIf there is any more information I can provide to help just let me know.\n\nThanks,\nJeff\n" }, { "id": 155301258, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-155301258", "created_at": "2014-04-16T01:07:59Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 1", "body": "Comment 4 by Michael Curran <mick@... on 2014-04-16 01:07\nIn [19fd2681a64209b13999248659bde818f2a53246]:\n```CommitTicketReference repository=\"\" revision=\"19fd2681a64209b13999248659bde818f2a53246\"\nReverting a change from December 2009 commit 6c53a29d where IAccessible NVDAObject's name property was forced to contain content from IAccessibleText if there was no caret present.\n\nThis was supposed to allow focusable labels in Thunderbird to read nicer. However, this caused a long-standing issue where the content of alerts in web browsers would speak twice, and Thunderbird now seems to oddly expose a caret on the labels thus disabling the code change anyway.\nRemoving this code may possibly cause some other regressions as its very old. However, if regressions are found they should be handled specificly for each case, as clearly this code was too general.\n\nShould be a fix re #3481. May affect re #2442, #2745\n\n```\n```\n" }, { "id": 322100070, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-322100070", "created_at": "2017-08-14T04:53:01Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 2", "body": "@michaelDCurran Could you please restate the implications of your https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-155301258 on this ticket more concisely? I don't think I follow this correctly, although I am a triager/user and no developer." }, { "id": 339435797, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-339435797", "created_at": "2017-10-25T18:59:45Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 3", "body": "Does anyone have an work around for this? Just as the OP stated (at least five years ago to the day? weird) Firefox ignores the addition of `role=\"alert\"` to a div on a page we're developing. It does not read the alert. " }, { "id": 489183277, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-489183277", "created_at": "2019-05-03T17:51:36Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 4", "body": "@contentfree, @javis, is this still an issue with NVDA 2019.1.1 and Firefox 66 or nightly? I think I cannot really reproduce this. Do you have an example website which shows this behavior?" }, { "id": 524251197, "url": "https://github.com/nvaccess/nvda/issues/2745#issuecomment-524251197", "created_at": "2019-08-23T09:47:59Z", "updated_at": null, "author": "Participant 4", "body": "Last reminder before closing this issue as abandoned. I can see that the author took the time to understand the CF role and write each post custom.  That's not spam.  Spam would generally have the same text verbatim, but then possibly add some gibberish to go undetected.  But in this case each message was manually composed by a human.\r\n\r\nSo from where I sit, the abuse seems to be on the part of whoever controlled @unnaturalname.  I say \"seems\" because I don't really know how he was controlled, but I now see a *ghost* which implies his account was deleted.\r\n\r\n> Especially when you bump old issues sending notifications to maintainers and users\r\n\r\nIf the bug persists then I don't see the problem with necroposting.       "body": "> I have read this thread again and I see there are a lot of concerns about Cloudflare, but there is nothing to say what to do instead.\r\n\r\nI've not tried to dig up dirt on Netlify, but that's one possible answer.       "author": "Participant 12",
      "body": "Since my previous comment, I have migrated from Cloudflare to Gandi LiveDNS (my registrar). It's not entirely painless process, but here are the general steps:\r\n\r\n1. Disable DNSSEC at Cloudflare and Gandi if it was enabled. Cloudflare will say that they will disable it when the records are removed from Gandi who will recommend you to **not change your DNS servers for 72 hours!**\r\n    * I don't know if this is actually necessary, but I didn't find that much instructions on how to transfer DNS with DNSSEC enabled domain and decided that the safest route is disabling DNSSEC at the old provider and enabling it on the new one.\r\n2. Export your DNS zone in advanced DNS settings at Cloudflare.\r\n3. Import the zone to Gandi by editing some parts by hand (SOA and especially TTLs). Cloudflare will have TTLs set to 1 for domains with DDoS protection and Gandi's minimum is 300. This confused me, because Gandi only gave unclear error messages, but I have sent them feedback.\r\n4. Restore DNSSEC as Cloudflare isn't the only one providing one-click-DNSSEC anymore :purple_heart: \r\n\r\nIn case of IPFS, I changed my IPFS gateway variables from cloudflare-ipfs.com to ipns.co ([GitHub repo](https://github.com/VanVan/ipfsProxyHTTP))."

      "author": "Participant 9",
      "body": "Subjecting visitors to CF is worse than subjecting them to bad performance.  So it was a good move.  \r\n\r\nI have some performance optimization suggestions:\r\n* [Specify](https://varvy.com/pagespeed/image-dimensions.html) the dimensions of all the images, so the important textual content can render before images are retrieved.\r\n* Link all the graphics to the sites they refer to offload the work of your server.  PTIO is promoting them, the least they can do is serve their own branded logos.\r\n* Any images that can't be linked to external sites could be isolated to a separate PTIO host. With the current solution we can guarantee that there’s no access logging for web visitors. \r\n\r\nWhen I say we took a performance hit, it wasn’t that bad. Of course there was going to be a difference between a single server in Germany vs a network of hundreds of servers internationally serving our content, but we do have a high performance server and like you said, I think the trade-off was worth it to move off CloudFlare. \r\n\r\nI’m pretty happy with the results so far :)\r\n\r\nWe have our own Searx instance now, I’ll probably just link to that or a list of public instances once we get ours listed in more places. \r\n\r\nRegarding everything else, probably best if you open a separate issue for them, like PayPal. With luck their employer has read the hypothetical privacyToolsIO4Biz pages which detail how to run a privacy-respecting corporation including single-sign-on / cloud storage / collaboration apps / etc.  But the *employer* or more usually the employer's sysadmin, are not \"the masses\" in any sense, though they are individuals and citizens. \r\n\r\nThe masses do not typically need to find a way to file an issue in any git repo, either, whether it be on github or on gitlab or on codeberg or on notabug or self-hosted.  Because that is a bit of a weird thing to do.  But also because there are usually half a dozen other venues, sometime over a dozen.  \r\n\r\n>  [the newly-created partially-transplanted community at the newly-relocated repo] will be allowed to grow to include privacy-aware PTIO contributors who (quite rightly) do not use Github\r\n\r\nIn some ways you are the counterpoint here, because you use github despite being privacy-aware... and really, *because* you are privacy-aware.  But there are other venues:  mastodon instance, matrix chatroom, self-hosted by privacy-respecting people.  Who are already cross-posting things brought up in those areas, here to github.  Mikaela just posted something from the matrixChatroom where somebody had suggested \"libre videogames\" listings.  JonahAragon posted something similar, which was from an email-conversation (which is Not An Official Way to contact the project-maintainers because it does not scale... so dear readership please do not use that mechanism... but it does function as a fallback option of last resort methinks).  \r\n\r\nThe main question is not, how many people will we attract if we selfhost a gitlab-instance that refuse to use github... the main question is, are there benefits to gitlabSelfhosting that are impossible to achieve on github + mastodonSelfhosted + matrixHomeserver + reddit + twitter + maybeFacebook + discourseSelfhosted + keybase + lastResortFallbackToEmail?  I think the number of people that refuse to use **any** of those existing options, but *would* suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted, is going to be dwarfed by the number of people that would stop contributing during the repo-switcheroo-shuffle because of hassle and switching costs and increased friction.  \r\n\r\np.s.  There is a different but related problem, which is that somewhere between six and nine official-or-quasi-official contact methods exist.  \r\n\r\n<details><summary>bifurcation of the overall privacy-community considered harmful</summary><p>\r\n\r\nAnd they all seem to be \"equal priority\" ...this bifurcates the overall community into tiny subcommunity-groupings and is a problem because there is no 'one main place' where everybody gathers habitually, plus 'specialized niche places' where particular sorts of work are done.  \r\n\r\nGoing out on a limb here, I think the One Main Place is probably going to be the discourseSelfhosted because it is most conducive to long-running async discussions, complemented by a github-associated wiki (or maybe a selfhosted wiki.js which is arguably cooler) where the *results* of discussions are summarized and stored.  Github issue-tracker is sub-optimal for discussion-threads because every comment emails a repo-watcher.  \r\n\r\nI think the chatroom area is fine for \"quick questions\" but unsuited to long involved discussions that happen over the course of many days.  I don't see keybase and keybaseChat as viable for any major role, though there is nothing wrong with the people that are code-signing the privacyToolsIO-branded online-services offerings being listed therein.  Similarly I don't think email directly to individual privacyToolsIO project-maintainers is a good plan... \r\n\r\nthat said, I would definitely signup for a daily&weekly BCC'd tips email-newletter and news-digest-blast, rather than get twitter&facebook versions of those things.  As long as privacyToolsIO mailing-lists are one-way info-blasts rather than bidirectional-conversations, that will keep the community from bifurcating needlessly (discussions of blasts will happen in discourseSelfHosted or in chatroom or whatnot -- each blast can link to an open forum-area even).  And because they are just simple bcc-based blasts they can be end2end encrypted via tutanota and protonmail and any other encrypted-webmail-provider that privacyToolsIO wishes to mention in the listings.  \r\n\r\nI think that twitter + reddit + facebook should be places where education-blasts are sent out and new participants are recruited, but should generally be privacy-propaganda-mouthpieces rather than \"community\" areas.  We don't want people on twitter talking about privacy, we just want to alert them via twitter and then help them transition to mastodon, ditto for alerting fbook denizens about friendica/diaspora, ditto for alerting reddit-participants to the new discourseSelfhosted.  And once they are signed up for encrypted webmail blasts, and transitioned to more privacy-respecting alternatives, they won't need to keep their twit/fbook/reddit thing around unless they want it for some strange reason :-) \r\n\r\n</p></details> \r\n"

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "> If at some point it makes sense to switch away from github to self-hosted gitlab-in-a-box run by the privacyToolsIO folks, that will some at an immediate cost in community-size.\r\n\r\nIt's short-sighted to only consider the short-term cost and neglect the long-term benefit of being able to attract contributors who value privacy and have a strong enough constitution to avoid MS Github.\r\n\r\n> Disagree, this is blowing things out of proportion -- you have filed your boycott-github request in the 'wrong' place\r\n\r\nBullshit.  The direct attack on a PTIO contributor (@unnaturalnamed) was an attack on the PTIO mission.  There are numerous privacy abuses outlined in the OP, all exposed in support of the mission, which you continually work against.  Most of your posts favor mass surveillance.  This is the mission statement:\r\n\r\n\"*You are being watched. Private and state-sponsored organizations are monitoring and recording your online activities. privacytools.io provides knowledge and tools to protect your privacy against global mass surveillance.*\"\r\n\r\nIt is your comment that is in the wrong place.\r\n\r\n## The \"we are excluded from our own mission\" line of reasoning\r\n> Github is not a \"recommended privacy tool\" on the site\r\n\r\nThis was already addressed in #868.  Leading by poor example is no way to educate users.  It's a recipe for disaster because it (rightly) also harms credibility.  If the experts cannot demonstrate making privacy-respecting choices it signals to others they will struggle even more with the same thing.  You seem to have no idea how easily laypeople are put off by security matters.  It's fragile, and you propose showing them that the experts can't handle it either.  It's a demoralizing approach.\r\n\r\n> The masses do not typically need to find a way to self-host a git repo.\r\n\r\nIt doesn't matter.  It's displayed on the website in a big box on the front page.  Every tool users see PTIO using or pimping is an implied endorsement of that tool whether you want it to be or not.  PTIO is not even saying \"do as we say not as we do\", leaving it for users to assume MS Github is socially responsible and privacy-respecting.  And it shows experts that PTIO staff is not committed to their own mission.\r\n\r\n> In some ways you are the counterpoint here, because you use github despite being privacy-aware\r\n\r\nYou've just supported paragraph 3 under \"Privacy-compromising consequence of using Github for the PTIO project\".\r\n\r\n> The main question is not, how many people will we attract if we selfhost a gitlab-instance that refuse to use github\r\n\r\nOf course it is.  You're asking the wrong questions.\r\n\r\n> the main question is, are there benefits to gitlabSelfhosting that are impossible to achieve on github + mastodonSelfhosted + matrixHomeserver + reddit + twitter + maybeFacebook + discourseSelfhosted + keybase + lastResortFallbackToEmail?\r\n\r\nNo it's not.  That's what you concern yourself with if you're actually looking for excuses to use tools that undermine the cause.  It's an attempt at trading integrity for misguided guesswork that users visiting the webpage and learning there that PTIO has a Facebook account will then reach other users, as opposed to finding PTIO within the FB walled-garden of mass surveillance.\r\n\r\nIt's also a betrayal when coupled with the statement \"*privacytools.io provides knowledge and tools to protect your privacy against global mass surveillance.*\"\r\n\r\n> I think the number of people that refuse to use any of those existing options, but would suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted, is going to be dwarfed by the number of people that would stop contributing during the repo-switcheroo-shuffle because of hassle and switching costs and increased friction.\r\n\r\nIt's the wrong question first of all, because only the \"would suddenly start using gitlabSelfhosted\" portion is relevant.  And whether it's \"sudden\" is over-stressed.  It's also short-sighted to blow an initial decrease out of proportion when the overall direction is commitment to the cause in a way that avoids hypocrisy.\r\n\r\nCredibility matters.\r\n"

      "id": 486810114,
      "url": "https://github.com/privacytoolsIO/privacytools.io/issues/843#issuecomment-486810114",
      "created_at": "2019-04-25T19:37:46Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-04-25T19:37:46Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "As usual, I think you misunderstand me:  you listed an issue called \"software removal:  github\".  The category of software-removal issues is intended for tools that are listed, which should no longer be listed.  You have filed such issues, as I recall ;-)  \r\n\r\nGithub is not software the privacyToolsIO recommends to the readership, it is just, some software that is *optionally* utilized by privacyToolsIO contributors:  thus, the correct title for this issue about \"boycott github\" does not belong in software-removal, that is the wrong place.  There is no category which matches what you are wanting, but if their was it would be called \"contributor-optional-software removal: github\" or something like that.  This is all I meant with the your-comment-is-in-the-wrong-place thing.  Try not to be so prickly please.  \r\n\r\n<details><summary>implied endorsement of a service owned by a firm that has political stances I dislike... that is no way to run a railroad, or a repo for that matter</summary><p>\r\n\r\nYou are pretty certain that @unnaturalname (no d at the end there) was not just marked as a spammer by the github algorithms, because they posted a bunch of identical issues in a row?  Because in the OP you say \"**Censorship** and PTIO project interference: Github staff **apparently** deleted a PTIO contributor.\"  But then later you change the story, and say \"The direct attack on a PTIO contributor (@unnaturalname<s>d</s>) was an attack on the PTIO mission.\"  \r\n\r\nWhere were they attacked?  Were they even censored?  Are you *sure* they were not just spamming a bunch of repos all across github, half a dozen on the 22nd and another half a dozen on the 26th, and got their github username auto-blocked?  Do you have an archive of the stuff they posted, prior to the alleged censorship?  And how do you leap from \"github removed a username\" to the \"github is directly attacking **the mission**\"?  Are you positive you want to make such leaps?  https://help.github.com/en/articles/github-terms-of-service#k-advertising-on-github  subsection 3, second sentence.  \r\n\r\nWe have a fundamental disagreement about what the mission of the privacyToolsIO website is, and of where the backend-tools used by contributors fit into that mission:  you think the main website is for everyday readership, and fantasize they will all install jami, if only you can delete all the competitors&alternatives to jami from the listings.  I have a more jaundiced view of humanity:  I know for an absolute fact that the everyday enduser cannot run linux-on-the-desktop, cannot flash their own lineageOS, and cannot handle ethereum-usernames and ringCx-hashnums for their messenger-app.  It is too much trouble, too much hassle, requires some tech-wizardry.  \r\n\r\nBy stark contrast, I also know for an absolute fact that everyday endusers *CAN* install and use firefox, signalapp, etc.  To you those projects are evil incarnate, and you don't understand why everybody just does not hand-compile ungoogledChromium and memorize their RingCx hashnum and use debian-for-the-desktop and stop owning a phone.  The reason is simple:  it is too hard, too much trouble/hassle/etc.  \r\n\r\nOur disagreement with respect to github is different, but has the same root cause:  you could care less about how much hassle and trouble and disruption and *loss of participation* getting rid of github and switching over to an entirely new issue-tracker and versioning-repo will cause.  To you, any amount of hassle is justified, because you fantasize that there are millions of contributors that refuse to utilize github on political grounds, and if only privacyToolsIO was not using evil github, those contributors would start to contribute.  \r\n\r\nBut this is nonsense:  contributions are officially accepted via federated mastodon, federated riotIM, reddit, twitter, self-hosted discourse, **and** github.  I've seen project-owners open issues on behalf of commentary in other places, too, this is not handwaving.  Contributors that refuse to use *any* of those options, are so few in number, they will never make up for the loss of github-contributors, and thus, leaving github is a bad decision on practical grounds.  \r\n\r\n>  Every tool users see PTIO using or pimping is an implied endorsement\r\n\r\nYou don't care about practical grounds, to you it is all about political guilt-by-association.  Microsoft drug-tests their employees, and the war on drugs is a bad political stance, and microsoft also owns github, and privacyToolsIO has some files hosted on github, and that means privacyToolsIO is practically endorsing the DEA no-knock dawn-raids... or something like that.  \r\n\r\nThis is not about privacy-respecting tools, this is purely about boycott-the-firms-that-I-dislike.  If you want to boycott them, do so,  If you see anybody who refuses to follow your lead and join your boycott, as your enemy, then that is your error, your loss.  \r\n\r\n> when the overall direction is commitment to the cause\r\n\r\nYou are talking about boycott of a supplier-of-supplier as being \"implied endorsement\" and conflating that with \"the cause\" aka the mission of the site.  The mission of the site is educating people about privacy, and recommending privacy-respecting tools.  \r\n\r\n> blowing an initial decrease out of proportion \r\n\r\nNo, it is looking at the practical impact of your boycott suggestion... and the ramifications thereof, such as, what happens when SomeNewPoliticallyOrientedRepoService arises that you like *even better than notabug*?  In this very thread, you have gone from rejecting github-and-gitlab while trumpeting notabug, to liking codeberg ... liking it so much, that you would want to switch over to it, should the notabug people have any political transgressions, during 2020.  \r\n\r\nWhich means yet another big switchover, yet another loss of contributor-community size, and that won't be the end of it either, because a **really** really really good service will come out in 2021, and so on.  Tool churn is bad enough in enduser-recommentations, but tool-churn on the backend where the site is built, has realworld pragmatic downsides. \r\n\r\n>  socially responsible\r\n>  trading integrity for misguided guesswork\r\n>  also a betrayal [of the mission] \r\n\r\nUh huh.  You are confusing political integrity, of your own view of how privacyToolsIO functions on the backend (where the repo is hosted in this case), with the integrity **of the listings** in the eyes of everyday readership.  \r\n\r\n>  You've just supported paragraph 3 under \"Privacy-compromising \r\n>  consequence [for libBletchey personally] of using Github for the PTIO project\".\r\n\r\nAnd you are confusing yourself personally, with \"The Mission\".  When you read the mission, it is very clear that you interpret it as 'tools to protect **your** privacy' being aimed at you personally.  But I don't think you are the only audience of the website.  You are a person who runs linux on the desktop, noscript-or-equivalent in your browser, spends a lot of time avoiding phones and phone-number-related tracking (up to and including travel to purchase a simcard not associated with your identity), and cares enough about privacy to spend a lot of hours online fighting mass surveillance.  \r\n\r\nBut I don't think the audience of www.privacyTools.io *is* just us wizard-level-three type folks.  You claim to also believe that:  you want the tool-recommendations to be suitable for use by the masses.  So we agree, at least, in theory.  But github is not a tool-recommendation to the masses.  It isn't being recommended to them.  \r\n\r\n>  Most of your posts favor mass surveillance.\r\n\r\nThere is little to say here.  As often happens with your attempts to attack a tool, that for whatever reason you personally dislike, and in whatever way you think will best discredit the tool and/or best discredit people that disagree with you -- as usual, you don't know what you are talking about.  \r\n\r\n>  it shows advanced users \r\n\r\nRight... \"advanced users\" meaning you and all the people that are just like you (people that demand everybody boycott github and treat anybody who does not as just-as-evil-as-billg).  People that don't understand logical fallacies, in other words.  People for whom the ends justify the means, *any* means, in other words.  \r\n\r\n>  that PTIO staff is not committed to their own mission\r\n\r\nNo, it shows you cannot comprehend the mission, because you don't see any distinction between yourself and people of your mindset, and the intended audience of the website.  Which is everyday readership that needs to be more educated about privacy:  people that are using Windows10, people that are using Chrome, people that are using Gmail, people that are on Facebook, people that are using WeChat or Whatsapp or unencrypted SMS.  \r\n\r\nBoycott-github because guilt-by-association, is ***so*** far from being relevant to that slice of the readership -- aka the majority of humanity -- it is almost unfathomable that you are really confused here.  You run Debian, UngoogledChromium, NeoMutt, Fediverse, and Jami or Wireapp.  Even though wireapp is on AWS ... you made a pragmatic decision that you wanted to be able to talk to your mother.  You are here, on github, and you made a pragmatic decision -- even though it runs on AWS and even though Microsoft owns it and drug-tests their employees -- to **be here** on github, fighting mass surveillance.  I think those are good decisions that you made, without exception.  All of them are fine choices.  \r\n\r\nThe only downside here is that you want everybody to follow your lead.  You want to boycott github, even though you didn't want to boycott github back when you signed up.  Because circumstances have changed, and you believe notabug is \"just as good\" despite the \"minor downsides\".  You believe that there will be a vast influx of notabug contributors, VAST influx, completely overcoming the loss of contributor-community when github is boycott'd.  \r\n\r\nHere is my advice:  if you can get your mom and ten of her over-age-fifty friends, to all hand-compile their own ungoogledChromium, to install (without your doing it for them) their own Linux-for-the-desktop distro onto all their x86-based systems, stop using anything but neoMutt for their email needs, delete their facebook/twitter/amazonDotCom/Microsoft/gmail accounts and entirely switch over to the fediverse, and stop using PSTN/fbookMsgr/skype/wechat/whatsapp/wireapp/signalapp and completely go cold-turkey Jami or Tox or nothing, then I will believe you that the everyday endusers are ready to boycott github.  Heck, ***I*** will immediately boycott github, if you can manage that.  \r\n\r\nUnless your mom works at CERN as a nuclear physicist or something, I'm assuming here that your mom is an everyday person ;-)  But you won't be able to do it.  For yourself:  yes, sure, I believe you can do it.  But not for a dozen everyday people born when the Berlin Wall was still standing; no chance.  I've spent a lot of years trying to get people to not give their friends and relatives into the maw of facebook, stop running windows when all they really need is LibreOffice, stop using gmail when protonmail or tutanota is good enough, and pick smartphone handsets that allow them to install software they can get a modicum of trust whilst using.  I have failed, that entire time, by and large.  Not for myself, but I'm willing to go the extra mile... most people are not willing.  \r\n\r\nThe tide is shifting though:  there is starting to be a backlash.  Everyday people are starting to think... hey maybe I don't have anything MUCH to hide, but does that mean I want everything I do and everyone I ever contact, to be spied upon by shady overlords?  PrivacyToolsIO is here to *help them upgrade their tools* and to educate them about the broad issues.  It is not here to insist they hand-compile UngoogledChromium or they are evil, it is not here to say \"if you run windows you are implicitly endorsing github so you are an enemy of privacy and a friend of mass surveillance.\"  That is [insert appropriate term].  \r\n\r\n</p></details>\r\n\r\nGithub is just one of half-a-dozen options, for the hardcore folks like ourselves that really care about privacy, to contribute on the backend.  If you really cannot ethically stand contributing on github, which is hosted on AWS, and which is owned by a corporation which drug-tests their employees, then you have a bunch of other options:  mastodon, discourse selfhosted at forum.privacytools.io ... et cetera.  You can stay here, and that is making a pragmatic choice:  you want to be involved directly on github-threads, rather than only being able to indirectly comment via riotim.privacytools.io chatrooms, and you want your words to be visible in google and bing and other non-privacy-respecting search engines.  Well, okay then, do that then.  \r\n\r\nBut pretending that it is only 'guesswork' to predict that switching around the repo and the issue-list from provider to provider to provider, will have a detrimental effect (vastly dwarfing any hypothetical salutory effect)... not to mention the opportunity cost where the project-maintainers have to spend a bunch of time and effort on the move to yet another new backend system rather than on improving the listing... no, that is not going to fly.  "

  "api_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358",
  "title": "Cookie consent options",
  "body": "<!-- Have you searched for similar issues on the repository?\r\nBefore submitting this issue, please visit our wiki for common ones: https://github.com/brave/browser-ios/wiki\r\nFor more, check out our community site: https://community.brave.com/ -->\r\n\r\n### Description: \r\nIn the EU, almost every website displays a pop up asking users to agree to their cookies. As a user this is v annoying. \r\nThere are many product that offer this consent management, one being Quantcast Choice (https://www.quantcast.com/gdpr/consent-management-solution/)\r\n\r\nCan we have an option in Privacy that allows users to not see these pop-ups?\r\nThe text can be something like: \r\nHide Cookie consent pop-ups\r\n\r\n\r\ncc @johnnyryan and @tomlowenthal for approval\r\n\r\n\r\n",
  "author": "Participant 1",
  "created_at": "2019-08-08T21:55:30Z",
  "updated_at": "2022-11-02T13:51:56Z",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": null,
  "issue_fetched_at": "2026-11-05T07:21:32.070556+00:00",

  ],

  "comments_complete": false,
  "comments": [
    {
      "id": 519702640,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-519702640",
      "created_at": "2019-08-08T21:58:07Z",

      "body": "Might be better as a shield?"

      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-520458859",
      "created_at": "2019-08-12T14:53:48Z",

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I answered on Slack in this thread https://bravesoftware.slack.com/archives/C4EE00THC/p1565345327108900?thread_ts=1565340552.108800&cid=C4EE00THC"
    },
    {
      "id": 550506607,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-550506607",
      "created_at": "2019-11-06T21:24:01Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-06T21:24:00Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "See: https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/5318\r\nfor more info"
    },
    {
      "id": 552617737,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-552617737",
      "created_at": "2019-11-11T21:11:50Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-11T21:11:49Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "1. Needs design: Where is this going? Is it a shield? \r\n    - If it is a shield, will it be domain level with a master switch as other shields are (i.e. user can enable it for _N_ site, or enable it for all and disable it for _N_ site, etc.)\r\n    - If it isn't a shield, will it be a master toggle for all web pages such as \"Block all Cookies\" and \"Private Browsing Only\"\r\n2. Needs info: \r\n    - What lists are we using, are they using CSS rules?\r\n    - Do we have the necessary support in https://github.com/brave/ab2cb to support converting these rules correctly?\r\n    - Do these lists need to be maintained and therefore added to the pipeline which converts rules and uploads them to the adblock s3 bucket? (which is not yet fixed btw: https://github.com/brave/devops/issues/1658)"
    },
    {
      "id": 553125167,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-553125167",
      "created_at": "2019-11-12T21:33:25Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-12T21:33:25Z",
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "\"Block Cookie Dialogs\" toggle in settings under \"Block all Cookies\""
    },
    {
      "id": 553125393,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-553125393",
      "created_at": "2019-11-12T21:34:00Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-12T21:33:59Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "The settings text is: \r\nUnder **Block all Cookies**\r\n_add_\r\nBock Cookie Dialogs (On|Off)\r\n\r\n@snyderp can you please reply to @kylehickinson on 2) Needs info above. \r\nThanks\r\n\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 553129666,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-553129666",
      "created_at": "2019-11-12T21:44:12Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-12T21:44:12Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@kylehickinson there are two (2.5?) approaches here broadly:\r\n\r\n1) Do what Cliqz is doing and just auto tell the IAB the user doesn't consent by setting those cookies for users.  This has a bunch of nasty side effects, including it _undoes_ a lot of our 3p cookie protections (since need to notify these folks, via 3p cookie, that the user has opted out).  We'd need to punch a hole in shields (not impossible, but something to be very cautious about…).  It also wouldn't address non IAB folks, and other similar popups\r\n\r\n2) Do what @ryanbr does with [his anti-cookie message list](https://www.fanboy.co.nz/fanboy-cookiemonster.txt), which is basically block as much related to the whole system as possible, at any possible vantage point (cosmetic, network, etc).  This has the benefit of being pretty easy to deply given our current infrastructure, but I think would cut against  @johnnyryan's legal concerns (it also has the typical coverage concerns of filter lists, but thats a \"solveable problem\" [hand wave])\r\n\r\nThere are a couple of hybrid options we could consider\r\n- Still keep the 3p cookie blocking with shields (e.g. don't punch an IAB sized hole in them) but just have the browser inject the relevant cookie into those network requests.\r\n\r\n- go hard on the filter lists, i can build up automation to target these kinds of annoyances.  Would be an interesting Brave distinguishing feature (again assuming it doesn't make us go to jail, re @johnnyryan jkjkjkjkj)\r\n\r\nIf none of those appeal, let me know and I can keep brainstorming"
    },
    {
      "id": 553144332,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-553144332",
      "created_at": "2019-11-12T22:22:28Z",
      "updated_at": "2019-11-12T22:22:28Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "We plan on doing 2 @snyderp for now. \r\n\r\n@kylehickinson wants to know about the list and has it been set up for iOS, converted etc. He can explain more. "
    },
    {
      "id": 578452012,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-578452012",
      "created_at": "2020-01-25T23:13:49Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-25T23:13:48Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "Submitted 2 PR's, to replace Prebake (the exisiting cookie list in `brave://adblock`), given prebake hasn't been updated since 2018. \r\n\r\nhttps://github.com/brave/adblock-rust/pull/67\r\nhttps://github.com/brave/brave-core/pull/4431"
    },
    {
      "id": 578898772,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-578898772",
      "created_at": "2020-01-27T18:57:42Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-27T18:57:41Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "@ryanbr just to double check, these new lists target cookie consent dialogs, or the whole wider set of dialogs (GDPR, CPAA, cookies, etc)?\r\n\r\n@kylehickinson these are not currently pulled into iOS at all.  Should they be?"
    },
    {
      "id": 578901059,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-578901059",
      "created_at": "2020-01-27T19:02:51Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-27T19:02:50Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "@snyderp We don't currently convert cosmetic rules in ab2cb, if we pull in these lists at the moment, it'll only block loads. If that's fine, we can pull them in. Otherwise we will have to first update ab2cb to convert cosmetic rules as well (including testing these)"
    },
    {
      "id": 578901515,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-578901515",
      "created_at": "2020-01-27T19:03:56Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-27T19:03:56Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "> If that's fine…\r\n\r\nI think that'll have to be a decision the iOS team makes.\r\n\r\n> update ab2cb…\r\n\r\nI think this would be a good capability to have, even if we don't fully exercise it right now"
    },
    {
      "id": 578903059,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-578903059",
      "created_at": "2020-01-27T19:07:36Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-27T19:07:36Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "☝️ cc @brave/ios @anthonypkeane "
    },
    {
      "id": 579020331,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-579020331",
      "created_at": "2020-01-28T00:21:05Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-28T00:21:05Z",
      "author": "Participant 7",
      "body": "@snyderp Like current prebake list, the Easylist cookie list will just hide the cookie div messages/consent dialogs.  \r\n\r\nSome sites can't be fixed due to cookies being checked by a website (see: quantcast messages). "
    },
    {
      "id": 580032434,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-580032434",
      "created_at": "2020-01-30T00:46:18Z",
      "updated_at": "2020-01-30T00:46:18Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "For a setting add \r\n\r\nBlock Cookie Dialogs toggle in settings under Block all Cookies\r\nDefault is On"
    },
    {
      "id": 765094992,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-765094992",
      "created_at": "2021-01-22T03:25:19Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-01-22T03:25:19Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Hi @pes10k Has there been a decision on whether we are doing this?"
    },
    {
      "id": 765100042,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-765100042",
      "created_at": "2021-01-22T03:42:21Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-01-22T03:42:21Z",
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "There is no short term iOS plan currently.  In brave-core, the immediate option is for users to enable the cookie blocking filter list in brave://adblock (knowing it comes with some webcompat risk).  The longer term option is to build smaller, higher confidence list we can check through automation.\r\n\r\nFor iOS the possible paths i can see are either:\r\n1. enable custom filter lists on iOS (so that iOS users can enable the same useful-but-sometimes-webcompat-risking), and / or\r\n2. wait until we have a higher confidence list (no immediate time frame) and we can incorporate that into the default iOS filter lists"
    },
    {
      "id": 845337571,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-845337571",
      "created_at": "2021-05-20T17:50:07Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-05-20T17:50:06Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Hi @pes10k \r\nDo you know if there has been any update on either 1 or 2 above? Thanks"
    },
    {
      "id": 845639792,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-845639792",
      "created_at": "2021-05-21T04:13:08Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-05-21T04:13:08Z",
      "author": "Participant 8",
      "body": "GPC, and the fanboy notification lists are the closest we've done at this point.  My sense is that adding the fanboy cookies list would add non-trivial compat risk, and would only be partially useful without cosmetic filtering on iOS.\r\n\r\nmy suggestion for how to proceed here is:\r\n1. implement cosmetic filtering on iOS\r\n2. add custom filter list support on iOS\r\n\r\nMy understanding is that neither have been implemented on iOS; i do not know what the current timeline is for those features"
    },
    {
      "id": 846129627,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-846129627",
      "created_at": "2021-05-21T17:43:41Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-05-21T17:43:41Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Linked to\r\n\r\nhttps://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/2683\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 850573655,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-850573655",
      "created_at": "2021-05-28T17:46:01Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-05-28T17:46:01Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "Given the comment on https://github.com/brave/brave-browser/issues/5318#issuecomment-849375469 it seems we can now implement an option to not show the cookie dialogue to users. \r\n\r\nUnder DISPLAY\r\nShow Cookie Consent Dialogues? (On/Off)\r\nEnabling this setting aims to prevent websites from asking you to consent to their cookies\r\n\r\nDefault off for now\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 850582378,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-850582378",
      "created_at": "2021-05-28T18:03:26Z",
      "updated_at": "2021-05-28T18:03:26Z",
      "author": "Participant 5",
      "body": "Blocked by #2683"
    },
    {
      "id": 1122507159,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-1122507159",
      "created_at": "2022-05-10T14:56:18Z",
      "updated_at": "2022-05-10T14:56:18Z",
      "author": "Participant 9",
      "body": "Hello,this feature would save a lot of time for European users and #2683 is closed, thus not blocking anymore.\nIs it possible to unblock it?\nThanks a lot!"
    },
    {
      "id": 1309472376,
      "url": "https://github.com/brave/brave-ios/issues/1358#issuecomment-1309472376",

    }

  "title": "Switch to open source map service",
  "body": "Wire is fantastic, finally, after a very long time of searching for a FOSS, encrypted chat service I've found one I can use and recommend. Thank you!\r\n\r\nBut I find it curious that a service where privacy and security is a key part, even to the point where you let us download the apk directly if we don't use Google Play Store (thank you for that!) still use Google Maps for your mapping feature. I don't want Google to know more about me/everyone than they already do, including places I'm interested in.\r\n\r\nPlease:\r\n\r\n1. Let me use the map feature without Google Play Services\r\n2. Stop sending those who click on a map link on desktop/web to Google Maps and switch to OpenStreetMaps or someone who uses data from OSM.\r\n3. Let those who click on a map link in Android choose which map app to open.\r\n\r\nThanks again!",

      "body": "@forteller while we wait for this enhancement, I highly suggest using https://microg.org/download.html.  If you build AOSP from source you just have to apply the patches @microg supplies to enable signature spoofing. Otherwise if you use Xposed (which defeats the purpose of ensuring privacy) you can install the signature spoofing module from there.  \r\n\r\nmicroG Pro Tip: Use the latest preview release, otherwise apps that use the newer version of Google Play Services will complain about your Play Services being out of date. I try to keep a strictly FOSS device but find myself occassionally downloading proprietary developed or distributed software for temporary usage with @yeriomin's https://github.com/yeriomin/YalpStore (Slack for work, Juno, an Uber-like service currently only in NYC, and now Wire)\r\n\r\nOff-topic:\r\n@wireapp needs to make it a priority to get this client to the point where it can be submitted to F-Droid. Any usage of a Google's proprietary services (distribution or jars) negates any claim of full-privacy.  You have no idea what their library is doing and it's more than probably it is fingerprinting devices and calling home.\r\n\r\nI had to install the mobile client due to conversation history \"feature\" which has caused lost messages because I proactively clear my browser's cookies, cache and storage. "
    },
    {

      "body": "Thanks for all the info! I understand that changes like this will take time, but I'm thinking that just changing what website people who click on the link is sent to should be quite trivial?\r\n\r\nOther than that, I'm sure you agree with me that microg is just an option for the nerdiest of the nerds and we need to make secure and privacy friendly systems that everyone can use, because even us nerds who care enough to use microg etc. are not safe if the wast majority of people are not safe. We all live in a society. :)"
    },
    {
      "id": 288733922,

It's not a webview,  the are using the Google Play Services maps class [https://github.com/wireapp/wire-android/blob/master/app/src/main/res/layout/fragment_location.xml], which makes replacing it exponentially more difficult and time consuming than just changing a url."
    },

      "id": 288809831,

      "updated_at": "2017-03-23T18:03:20Z",
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Yes, that's the feature I'm talking about. But if you receive one of those shared locations and you use Wire on desktop you are sent to maps.google.com in your browser. That's the link I'm talking about.\r\n\r\nAlso, just noticed: When clicking on it on Android, the Google Maps app opens up directly. I have it installed, unfortunately, but I'm not accepting the terms of service and won't use it. Instead we should be asked which mapps app we want to open the link in."
    },

      "id": 288816166,
      "url": "https://github.com/wireapp/wire-android/issues/734#issuecomment-288816166",

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Yes, exactly. I've updated the issue to try to make my intention clearer, and also added a third point for those receiving a map link on Android."
    },
    {
      "id": 310024978,
      "url": "https://github.com/wireapp/wire-android/issues/734#issuecomment-310024978",
      "created_at": "2017-06-21T09:35:09Z",
      "updated_at": "2017-06-21T09:35:09Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "The real issue here, IMO, is that instead of sending the location in a standardized neutral format that can be opened with whatever program you like, for instance OSMAnd on Android, it sends out links to the Google maps online service. The right way to do this would be to use the [GEO URI format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geo_URI_scheme). Another additional convenience format would be a provider-independent web link."
    },

  "body": "When logging objects to the API logs, add functionality to filter out certain keys so that they never get logged. Here is a starter list, to which we should be able to add more in the future:

## Acceptance Criteria:
- [x] Do not log:
- [x]   * token
- [x]   * headers.authorization (bearer token)
- [ ] remove instances where console.log(...) to use one of `applicationContext.logger`:
  - [ ] `.error('errorMessageHere', err)`: an error has occurred, log this and include an object for context
  - [ ] `.warn('highVolume', data)`: useful for logging warnings about activity. Include any relevant info in data
  - [ ] `.notice('userLogin', user)`: useful for metrics and auditing the application's activity
  - [ ] `.info('message here', data)`: not logged to production, but light debugging in lower environments
  - [ ] `.debug('verboseLog', data)`:  messages you want to see for the developer, will not be logged on deployed instance

## Note:
* There are 110 console logs. 
* Mike Marcotte to backlog any additional work needed for post-MVP.

**Product Owner**

**UX**

 - [ ] UI should be touch optimized and responsive for external only (functions on supported mobile devices and optimized for screen sizes as required)
 - [ ] Module dependencies are up-to-date and are at the latest resolvable version (npm update)
